newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas edges lower ahead of milder weather.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas edges lower ahead of milder weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices edged a little lower Wednesday as warmer air moved eastward, market sources said.
Louisiana Gulf prices fell another three cents to the mid-$1.80s per mmBtu, with Henry Hub quoted mostly at $1.86-1.89.
In south Texas, prices were similarly lower in the low-$1.80s as temperatures in the state remained a few degrees above normal. Cooler weather was forecast for early next week.
Gulf cash was still in convergence with NYMEX Henry Hub April natgas, which fell 1.3 cents to $1.884 at 1338 EST.
In the East, where temperatures were expected to moderate Thursday and Friday, New York city-gate prices fell more than five cents to the high-$2.20s to low-$2.30s.
Similarly in the Appalachian region, prices were down an average of eight cents to about $1.97-2.06.
In the Midcontinent, prices slipped another four cents to the low-to-mid $1.70s as forecasters said they expected temperatures to rise Thursday and into Friday.
Panhandle prices still carried about a two to three cent premium to prices on ANR, SW.
Chicago city-gate values slumped into the mid-to-high $1.90s, down more than five cents from Tuesday, while prices at the Detroit city-gate were only slightly lower at $2.10-2.12.
Despite some extended heat in the West, Permian prices tumbled five cents to the mid-$1.60s to about $1.70.
Temperatures in the Southwest, including southern California, are expected to hover 10 to 20 degrees Fahrenheit above normal through early next week.
The 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California was still in "hot standby" this morning and expected to restart today, the NRC reported.
Withdrawal estimates for today's American Gas Association storage report were mostly at 40-50 bcf, according to a Reuter poll.
